transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep losing important papers and tools I need for jobs, and it’s starting to hurt my business. Ever since my husband passed away and I had to take over all the administrative work, it has just been completely overwhelming. I'm really struggling to keep up with everything now.

Since your husband passed away, have you been feeling down most of the day or losing interest in things you usually enjoy? Or does it feel more like stress and overwhelm mainly tied to managing the business and paperwork?

It definitely feels more like stress and overwhelm tied to the paperwork rather than losing interest in things. I still really love the hands-on carpentry work, and that part still comes easily to me. It's just sitting down to handle the administrative tasks, invoices, and scheduling that feels completely overwhelming and paralyzing.

Since your husband died, have these stress and concentration problems been causing clear problems in your daily functioning beyond what you would expect from grief, like trouble managing basic responsibilities most days? Or does it feel more like a normal grieving reaction without major ongoing impairment?

It definitely feels like much more than just normal grief because it's causing major, constant disruptions in my daily work. Since I took over the office side a little over a year ago, my disorganization has led to late invoices, mixed-up job schedules, and frustrated clients. It's gotten completely unmanageable, and I'm really worried I won't be able to keep the business afloat.

Aside from the business paperwork, are these stress and concentration problems affecting other parts of your life too, like managing the household, paying bills, or keeping up with personal responsibilities? Or are they mainly limited to the new administrative duties you took over after your husband died?

It's not just the business—I'm constantly tearing the house apart looking for misplaced personal items, and I can't even sit quietly to relax with a book without getting incredibly fidgety. Looking back, I've actually had these tendencies since childhood, like losing homework and daydreaming, but they only became completely unmanageable after I had to take on the business admin load alone.

Before your husband passed away, did these attention and disorganization problems cause clear difficulties in school, work, or relationships across different settings, or did they only become a real problem after you took on the business paperwork?

While it only became a major crisis after my husband passed, I've actually struggled with organization and attention since childhood. In elementary school, I was always forgetting my homework, losing permission slips, and daydreaming through lessons. My teachers used to tell my parents that I was smart but just couldn't stay focused or organized.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of inattention/disorganization (losing homework, daydreaming, poor focus, losing important items) with hyperactivity/restlessness (cannot sit quietly, feels fidgety), now causing clinically significant impairment across work and home settings. Symptoms predate the spouse’s death and are not better explained by grief or a depressive syndrome, making ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation/hyperkinetic disorder the best fit among the provided candidates.
